questions.topic: License verification at commencement of employment
questions.trigger: A staffing agency sends a pharmacist to cover a Massachusetts pharmacy for the first time. The agency supplies a résumé and a copy of last year's license. When must the pharmacy verify that the pharmacist's license is current?
questions.legal_decision: Verify at commencement.
questions.critical_exception: Agency placement does not remove the pharmacy duty.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If current licensure is already verified at commencement, this requirement is met.
questions.stem: A staffing agency sends a pharmacist to cover a Massachusetts pharmacy for the first time. The agency supplies a résumé and a copy of last year's license. When must the pharmacy verify that the pharmacist's license is current?

choices.text: At the first annual pharmacy self-inspection.
choices.why: Incorrect. The self-inspection schedule does not replace commencement verification.

choices.text: At commencement of the pharmacist's employment.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacy must verify current licensure when employment begins.

choices.text: Within 14 days after the assignment begins.
choices.why: Incorrect. There is no such 14-day grace period in this provision.

choices.text: Within 30 days if the assignment continues.
choices.why: Incorrect. Temporary assignments do not create a 30-day exemption.

choices.text: At the next individual license renewal date.
choices.why: Incorrect. Renewal timing does not defer the employer's verification duty.

questions.topic: Certified technician communicates factual profile history
questions.trigger: Which information may a certified technician communicate to a prescriber without exercising professional judgment, after identifying as certified and obtaining pharmacist approval?
questions.legal_decision: Relay recorded factual information.
questions.critical_exception: Other legal restrictions still apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If interpretation or modification is needed, refer to an authorized professional.
questions.stem: Which information may a certified technician communicate to a prescriber without exercising professional judgment, after identifying as certified and obtaining pharmacist approval?

choices.text: A recommendation to reduce a patient's dose.
choices.why: Incorrect. Dose modification requires professional judgment.

choices.text: An assessment of the patient's therapeutic response.
choices.why: Incorrect. Therapeutic assessment is clinical judgment.

choices.text: An interpretation of a suspected drug interaction.
choices.why: Incorrect. Clinical conflict resolution exceeds technician authority.

choices.text: Dates and strengths of recorded prescription fills.
choices.why: Correct. Factual profile information requiring no interpretation can be communicated.

choices.text: A recommendation to discontinue a patient's therapy.
choices.why: Incorrect. A therapy change is not authorized by this provision.

questions.topic: Hospital pharmacy eligible employee household recipients
questions.trigger: A hospital pharmacy lacks a retail Drug Store pharmacy license. No additional statutory authority applies. Which individuals fall within the categories the hospital pharmacist may serve?
questions.legal_decision: Identify permitted hospital pharmacy recipients.
questions.critical_exception: Other law or a retail Drug Store license can change the analysis.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A child living in the employee's household is in the listed category.
questions.stem: A hospital pharmacy lacks a retail Drug Store pharmacy license. No additional statutory authority applies. Which individuals fall within the categories the hospital pharmacist may serve? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: An employee's spouse living in the employee's household.
choices.why: Correct. The same-household spouse is expressly included.

choices.text: An employee's adult child living in another household.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision requires the employee's child to live in the same household.

choices.text: A hospital outpatient receiving care at the hospital.
choices.why: Correct. Hospital outpatients are an authorized category.

choices.text: An employee who receives medical care elsewhere.
choices.why: Correct. Hospital employment itself is a qualifying category.

choices.text: An employee's parent living in the employee's household.
choices.why: Incorrect. The specified family categories are spouses and children, not parents.

questions.topic: Documenting exceptional work beyond ordinary hours
questions.trigger: At the end of a 12-hour shift, a pharmacist encounters an unexpected emergency in which leaving immediately would jeopardize patient care. No other pharmacist is available. What is required if the pharmacist continues under the extenuating-circumstances provision?
questions.legal_decision: Document the exception and minimize overtime.
questions.critical_exception: This is not a routine overtime permission.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without extenuating patient-interest circumstances, apply the usual hours/rest rule.
questions.stem: At the end of a 12-hour shift, a pharmacist encounters an unexpected emergency in which leaving immediately would jeopardize patient care. No other pharmacist is available. What is required if the pharmacist continues under the extenuating-circumstances provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Obtain a prospective waiver from the Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prospective waiver is not specified for this exception.

choices.text: Document the circumstances justifying the additional work.
choices.why: Correct. Documentation of the exceptional circumstances is mandatory.

choices.text: Minimize the working time beyond 12 hours.
choices.why: Correct. Excess time must be minimized.

choices.text: Schedule the same overtime for the next shift.
choices.why: Incorrect. A routine schedule is not itself a qualifying patient-care emergency.

choices.text: Substitute manager approval for written documentation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Approval does not replace the licensee's documentation duty.

questions.topic: Renewal after registration lapse exceeding two years
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacist's registration expired three years ago without suspension or revocation. Which examination does the renewal rule expressly require?
questions.legal_decision: Identify the mandatory exam for a lapse exceeding two years.
questions.critical_exception: Other Board conditions also apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For a lapse of more than 60 days but not more than two years, 4.02(4) governs rather than this examination mandate.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's registration expired three years ago without suspension or revocation. Which examination does the renewal rule expressly require?

choices.text: NAPLEX.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule for ordinary lapse does not expressly require NAPLEX.

choices.text: NAPLEX and MPJE.
choices.why: Incorrect. NAPLEX is not expressly required in this particular lapse provision.

choices.text: MPJE.
choices.why: Correct. The MPJE is required when the lapse exceeds two years.

choices.text: A pharmacy technician certification exam.
choices.why: Incorrect. Technician certification is not a pharmacist renewal exam.

choices.text: No examination if CE is complete.
choices.why: Incorrect. Continuing education does not waive the mandatory MPJE.

questions.trigger: What is the maximum number of Massachusetts pharmacist continuing education contact hours that may be earned in one calendar day?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish the daily cap from annual limits.
questions.critical_exception: Annual eligibility and specific content requirements still apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If ten hours are spread over separate days, the daily cap must be evaluated for each day.
questions.stem: What is the maximum number of Massachusetts pharmacist continuing education contact hours that may be earned in one calendar day?

choices.text: 5 hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Five is not the daily cap.

choices.text: 8 hours.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation caps earned CE at eight contact hours per calendar day.

choices.text: 10 hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Ten exceeds the daily cap.

choices.text: 15 hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fifteen is the annual home-study/mediated-instruction limit, not the daily cap.

choices.text: 20 hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Twenty is the ordinary annual total requirement, not the daily cap.

questions.topic: Trainee employment limit exceeded before age eighteen
questions.trigger: A licensed trainee worked 1,620 hours before turning 18 under the age exception. The trainee meets the technician application requirements and turns 18 on November 10. What application deadline applies?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the special post-birthday application deadline.
questions.critical_exception: The age exception allows exceeding the ordinary limits before 18.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If neither ordinary limit had been exceeded before age 18, this particular deadline would not be triggered.
questions.stem: A licensed trainee worked 1,620 hours before turning 18 under the age exception. The trainee meets the technician application requirements and turns 18 on November 10. What application deadline applies?

choices.text: Within 7 days of the birthday.
choices.why: Incorrect. Seven days is not the specified application period.

choices.text: Within 14 days of the birthday.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fourteen days is not the specified period.

choices.text: Within 30 days of the birthday.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation specifies 30 days after the 18th birthday.

choices.text: Within 60 days of the birthday.
choices.why: Incorrect. Sixty days exceeds the specified period.

choices.text: Within one year of the birthday.
choices.why: Incorrect. The one-year ordinary trainee limit is not this application period.

questions.trigger: What is the federal controlled-substance schedule of Sonata (zaleplon)?
questions.legal_decision: Identify a controlled hypnotic from its name.
questions.critical_exception: Therapeutic class alone does not establish scheduling.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A different hypnotic requires checking its own listing.
questions.stem: What is the federal controlled-substance schedule of Sonata (zaleplon)?

choices.text: Schedule II.
choices.why: Incorrect. Zaleplon is not in Schedule II.

choices.text: Schedule III.
choices.why: Incorrect. Zaleplon is not in Schedule III.

choices.text: Schedule IV.
choices.why: Correct. Zaleplon is listed as a Schedule IV depressant.

choices.text: Schedule V.
choices.why: Incorrect. Zaleplon is not in Schedule V.

choices.text: Not federally scheduled.
choices.why: Incorrect. Zaleplon is federally controlled.

questions.topic: Interstate Schedule IV prescription for local dispensing
questions.trigger: A Florida physician holds valid Florida prescribing authority and DEA registration. An adult patient will collect the physician's electronic lorazepam prescription at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which additional step applies to the Massachusetts pharmacist?
questions.legal_decision: Verify the interstate Schedule IV prescription.
questions.critical_exception: This is local collection, not interstate delivery.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For interstate Schedule VI, the express Schedule III–V verification requirement does not apply, but authenticity still must be assessed.
questions.stem: A Florida physician holds valid Florida prescribing authority and DEA registration. An adult patient will collect the physician's electronic lorazepam prescription at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which additional step applies to the Massachusetts pharmacist?

choices.text: Verify the prescription by telephone or other means.
choices.why: Correct. Section 18(c) specifically requires verification of interstate Schedule III–V prescriptions.

choices.text: Require the physician to obtain Massachusetts controlled substance registration.
choices.why: Incorrect. Qualifying out-of-state prescribers may issue these prescriptions without obtaining Massachusetts registration.

choices.text: Confirm the physician practices in a state bordering Massachusetts.
choices.why: Incorrect. That geographic restriction does not govern this Schedule IV in-person dispensing.

choices.text: Apply the five-day window for out-of-state Schedule II prescriptions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The five-day rule is not the applicable Schedule IV rule.

choices.text: Treat electronic network delivery as sufficient prescription verification.
choices.why: Incorrect. Electronic receipt alone does not discharge the verification requirement.

questions.trigger: A Massachusetts prescriber issues an otherwise valid prescription for 90 methylphenidate tablets, one daily. What is the general statutory maximum single-fill supply?
questions.legal_decision: Recognize the nonopioid 90-day single-fill exception.
questions.critical_exception: Other statutory and regulatory restrictions may apply; none are stated.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For ordinary Schedule II opioid analgesia outside another exception, the general cap is 30 days.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts prescriber issues an otherwise valid prescription for 90 methylphenidate tablets, one daily. What is the general statutory maximum single-fill supply?

choices.text: 14 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fourteen days is not this nonopioid quantity cap.

choices.text: 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. The general 30-day cap has a nonopioid exception.

choices.text: 60 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. The nonopioid exception is not 60 days.

choices.text: 90 days.
choices.why: Correct. The statute includes methylphenidate in the nonopioid 90-day category.

choices.text: 120 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. The general exception is capped at 90 days.

questions.trigger: A trained pharmacist offers contraceptive prescribing. A 16-year-old requests an authorized oral hormonal contraceptive, completes the required screening, and is clinically eligible. Which statements describe the Massachusetts prescribing pathway?
questions.legal_decision: Apply screening eligibility, supply cap and no-appointment pathway.
questions.critical_exception: Other applicable consent, training and clinical requirements still govern.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An ineligible product or patient requires a different lawful pathway.
questions.stem: A trained pharmacist offers contraceptive prescribing. A 16-year-old requests an authorized oral hormonal contraceptive, completes the required screening, and is clinically eligible. Which statements describe the Massachusetts prescribing pathway? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Age alone does not exclude the patient.
choices.why: Correct. The circular permits eligible patients of any age.

choices.text: A scheduled appointment is a prescribing prerequisite.
choices.why: Incorrect. The circular says a scheduled appointment must not be required.

choices.text: The prescription may authorize up to a 12-month supply.
choices.why: Correct. Twelve months is the stated maximum.

choices.text: Absence of a prior primary care visit does not preclude refills.
choices.why: Correct. The guidance expressly permits refills without a clinical visit.

choices.text: The patient must receive a written record of the product prescribed and dispensed.
choices.why: Correct. Providing the written record is a general requirement.

questions.citation: DCP 26-08-125, General Prescribing Requirements (e); Hormonal Contraceptive Patches and Oral Hormonal Contraceptives (a)–(d)

questions.trigger: A pharmacist is selecting training before independently prescribing HIV prevention medications under Massachusetts guidance. Which statements correctly describe the required preparation?
questions.legal_decision: Identify required HIV-specific training.
questions.critical_exception: Specified accreditation/credit and statewide guidance also apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A properly accredited course covering required topics and time can satisfy the training element.
questions.stem: A pharmacist is selecting training before independently prescribing HIV prevention medications under Massachusetts guidance. Which statements correctly describe the required preparation? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A course covering medication pharmacology alone qualifies.
choices.why: Incorrect. The circular specifically rejects pharmacology-only education.

choices.text: The training includes at least two hours on HIV prevention prescribing and related competencies.
choices.why: Correct. The circular specifies the minimum time and related content.

choices.text: The training addresses recognition of possible acute retroviral syndrome.
choices.why: Correct. Recognition of these symptoms is a specified component.

choices.text: A general immunization certificate replaces HIV-specific training.
choices.why: Incorrect. Immunization training alone does not meet the required content.

choices.text: Documentation of completed training is available upon request.
choices.why: Correct. Completion documentation must be supplied on request.

questions.citation: DCP 26-08-125, Human Immunodeficiency Virus Prevention (a),(b) and note

questions.topic: Age threshold for nonvaccine pharmacy administration
questions.trigger: A parent brings a 17-year-old for a prescribed single-dose intramuscular paliperidone palmitate injection. Pharmacy personnel meet the training requirements. No separate administration authority applies. What is the appropriate response?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the 18-year threshold.
questions.critical_exception: Other lawful administration authority is not asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: At 18 or older, age no longer bars the pathway, but other conditions remain.
questions.stem: A parent brings a 17-year-old for a prescribed single-dose intramuscular paliperidone palmitate injection. Pharmacy personnel meet the training requirements. No separate administration authority applies. What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Administer under the circular letter with the parent's written consent.
choices.why: Incorrect. Parental consent does not replace the age threshold.

choices.text: Refer elsewhere for administration because the patient is younger than 18.
choices.why: Correct. The dispensing-by-administration pathway applies to patients at least 18.

choices.text: Arrange administration by a supervised intern rather than a pharmacist.
choices.why: Incorrect. The age threshold applies to both professions.

choices.text: Administer after obtaining the prescriber's separate verbal authorization.
choices.why: Incorrect. Additional authorization does not remove the age restriction.

choices.text: Administer if the patient's parent is present throughout the procedure.
choices.why: Incorrect. Parent presence does not establish eligibility under the circular.

questions.citation: DCP 26-03-124, Dispensing by Administration; Medications Eligible for Pharmacist or Pharmacy Intern Administration

critical_error_options.reason: Administration under the circular to an age-ineligible patient.
Changing the administrator does not change eligibility.
Authorization alone does not remove the age restriction.
Parent presence does not remove age restriction.

questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacy prepares a standing order for routine vaccination. Which elements must the standing order address under the Board's vaccine policy?
questions.legal_decision: Identify required standing-order content.
questions.critical_exception: Other appendix elements also apply; the list is not exhaustive.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An order missing emergency procedures needs correction.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy prepares a standing order for routine vaccination. Which elements must the standing order address under the Board's vaccine policy? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Eligibility and exclusion criteria for vaccine recipients.
choices.why: Correct. The appendix requires inclusion and exclusion criteria.

choices.text: The retail price of each vaccine offered.
choices.why: Incorrect. The appendix does not require retail pricing.

choices.text: Emergency treatment and how to obtain further care.
choices.why: Correct. The appendix specifies emergency treatment and assistance for continued care.

choices.text: Timing, route and dose of the vaccines.
choices.why: Correct. These administration details are required.

choices.text: The signature of a duly authorized prescriber.
choices.why: Correct. An authorized prescriber signature is a required element.

questions.citation: Board Policy 2023-02, revised September 4, 2025, IX Appendix

questions.trigger: A pharmacy has a sound-insulated consultation room behind its prescription counter. Patients reach it only by walking through the dispensing area. What change addresses the Massachusetts consultation-area requirement?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the consultation-area accessibility requirement.
questions.critical_exception: Visual and auditory privacy and required signage remain necessary.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An appropriately private area accessed from outside the prescription area meets the access element.
questions.stem: A pharmacy has a sound-insulated consultation room behind its prescription counter. Patients reach it only by walking through the dispensing area. What change addresses the Massachusetts consultation-area requirement?

choices.text: Add a counseling-rights sign next to the consultation room entrance.
choices.why: Incorrect. Signage does not correct the route of access.

choices.text: Arrange for an employee to escort patients through the prescription area.
choices.why: Incorrect. Escorted passage through the dispensing area does not satisfy the rule.

choices.text: Provide direct access from outside the dispensing area.
choices.why: Correct. The room must be accessible without traversing the stockroom or dispensing area.

choices.text: Retain the current layout and provide counseling by appointment.
choices.why: Incorrect. Appointment timing does not correct the access requirement.

choices.text: Provide a remote counseling option instead of modifying the access route.
choices.why: Incorrect. A remote option does not replace the designated area requirement.

questions.topic: Returned multidrug single-dose package after therapy change
questions.trigger: A patient returns a multidrug single-dose compliance package previously dispensed by this pharmacy. The prescriber discontinued one drug and prescribed a replacement. All applicable repackaging safeguards can be met. Which action is permitted?
questions.legal_decision: Permit same-patient repackaging after therapy change.
questions.critical_exception: Removed drugs cannot be returned to inventory or dispensed to another patient.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An ordinary returned prescription outside the specified packaging exception is not eligible under this provision.
questions.stem: A patient returns a multidrug single-dose compliance package previously dispensed by this pharmacy. The prescriber discontinued one drug and prescribed a replacement. All applicable repackaging safeguards can be met. Which action is permitted?

choices.text: Replace the discontinued drug, relabel, and redispense to the same patient.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation permits this same-patient therapy-change repackaging pathway.

choices.text: Return the removed drug to general inventory after verifying the product identity.
choices.why: Incorrect. The removed drug may not return to inventory.

choices.text: Redispense the modified package to a different patient on the same regimen.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception is limited to the returning patient.

choices.text: Repackage for the same patient but preserve the original unmodified label.
choices.why: Incorrect. The package must be labeled in accordance with 9.08(5) before redispensing.

choices.text: Transfer the returned package to another pharmacy for routine inventory reuse.
choices.why: Incorrect. The same-patient exception is not general stock reuse authority.

questions.topic: HIPAA access request containing litigation material
questions.trigger: A HIPAA-covered pharmacy receives a request for a patient's dispensing records and a separate file compiled in reasonable anticipation of litigation. The dispensing records are in the designated record set. No other denial ground applies. Which actions comply with the federal access rule?
questions.legal_decision: Separate excluded material from accessible PHI.
questions.critical_exception: No other access-denial ground is asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Ordinary designated-record-set PHI does not qualify for the litigation-material exclusion merely because litigation exists.
questions.stem: A HIPAA-covered pharmacy receives a request for a patient's dispensing records and a separate file compiled in reasonable anticipation of litigation. The dispensing records are in the designated record set. No other denial ground applies. Which actions comply with the federal access rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Provide access to the ordinary dispensing records.
choices.why: Correct. Accessible underlying PHI remains subject to the right of access.

choices.text: Deny access to the entire request because it includes litigation material.
choices.why: Incorrect. A permissible partial denial does not justify withholding accessible PHI.

choices.text: Withhold the separate material prepared for the anticipated litigation.
choices.why: Correct. Litigation-prepared information is an express exception to the access right.

choices.text: Explain the partial denial in writing, including how to complain.
choices.why: Correct. The written denial must state the basis and applicable complaint information.

choices.text: Require the patient to explain the need for the dispensing records.
choices.why: Incorrect. A patient need not give a reason for access.

questions.citation: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)(ii),(d)(1)–(2); HHS Right of Access FAQ

questions.trigger: A patient needs a newly prescribed Schedule IV controlled substance but lacks government-issued identification. The pharmacist documents a credible serious hardship if the prescription is withheld. The patient is present. What additional action is required?
questions.legal_decision: Apply both hardship exception conditions.
questions.critical_exception: Hardship alone is insufficient; written name, address and signature are required.
questions.counterfactual_flip: With valid qualifying identification, the ordinary identification rule applies.
questions.stem: A patient needs a newly prescribed Schedule IV controlled substance but lacks government-issued identification. The pharmacist documents a credible serious hardship if the prescription is withheld. The patient is present. What additional action is required?

choices.text: Ask the patient to confirm their full name and home address orally.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule requires the specified record and signature.

choices.text: Record the identification number of an absent family member with permission.
choices.why: Incorrect. An absent person's identifier does not satisfy the exception.

choices.text: Ask the prescriber to send a separate fax identifying the patient.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prescriber fax does not replace the required alternate identity record.

choices.text: Have the patient print their name and address and sign the prescription or log.
choices.why: Correct. Together with documented hardship, this satisfies the alternate-identification condition.

choices.text: Have a second pharmacist sign a statement confirming the patient's identity.
choices.why: Incorrect. A pharmacist signature does not replace the required patient or agent signature.

critical_error_options.reason: Omission of required record and signature.

questions.trigger: An authorized Schedule IV refill transfer is completed. Which event starts the federal two-year transfer-record retention period?
questions.legal_decision: Identify the last-refill retention trigger.
questions.critical_exception: Any other applicable record-retention obligation still applies.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A different record category may have a different retention trigger.
questions.stem: An authorized Schedule IV refill transfer is completed. Which event starts the federal two-year transfer-record retention period?

choices.text: Original prescription issuance.

choices.text: First prescription filling.
choices.why: Incorrect. First filling is not the specified trigger.

choices.text: Last prescription refill.

choices.text: Date of prescription transfer.
choices.why: Incorrect. The transfer date is recorded but does not start this period.

choices.text: Patient profile creation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Profile creation is not relevant to this retention period.

questions.trigger: A new prescription will be delivered to a patient's home. The pharmacy system has clinical and billing alerts. Which findings are among the clinical issues Massachusetts requires the pharmacist to make a reasonable effort to identify during prospective DUR?
questions.legal_decision: Separate clinical prospective DUR from financial review.
questions.critical_exception: Delivery does not remove the duty to conduct appropriate DUR.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A clinically relevant duplication or other listed problem likewise requires appropriate evaluation and documented measures.
questions.stem: A new prescription will be delivered to a patient's home. The pharmacy system has clinical and billing alerts. Which findings are among the clinical issues Massachusetts requires the pharmacist to make a reasonable effort to identify during prospective DUR? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A drug interaction with a food the patient regularly consumes.
choices.why: Correct. Drug-food interactions are included.

choices.text: The patient's eligibility for a manufacturer copay program.
choices.why: Incorrect. Financial assistance eligibility is not a listed clinical DUR issue.

choices.text: A disease that contraindicates the prescribed drug.
choices.why: Correct. Drug-disease contraindications are included.

choices.text: A change in the patient's preferred pharmacy network.
choices.why: Incorrect. Network participation is not a listed clinical DUR issue.

choices.text: A requirement for a new insurance prior authorization.
choices.why: Incorrect. Coverage authorization is distinct from the specified clinical screening issues.

questions.trigger: On Monday at 10 a.m., a pharmacist dispenses 12 of 30 prescribed oxycodone tablets solely because of insufficient stock. The balance arrives Thursday at noon. Neither patient nor practitioner requested a partial fill. What does the federal rule require?
questions.legal_decision: Use 72 hours from the first shortage partial fill.
questions.critical_exception: No patient/practitioner request or LTCF/terminal-illness exception is asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Within 72 hours, the remainder can be dispensed if other validity conditions hold.
questions.stem: On Monday at 10 a.m., a pharmacist dispenses 12 of 30 prescribed oxycodone tablets solely because of insufficient stock. The balance arrives Thursday at noon. Neither patient nor practitioner requested a partial fill. What does the federal rule require?

choices.why: Incorrect. A Schedule II prescription cannot be refilled.

choices.text: Dispense the balance within seven days of the original partial filling.
choices.why: Incorrect. The shortage completion window is 72 hours, not seven days.

questions.topic: Schedule IV partial dispensing near six-month limit
questions.trigger: A valid Schedule IV prescription authorizes 60 tablets with no refills. It was issued five months ago; the pharmacy has dispensed 20 tablets in a partial filling. Which statements correctly describe additional partial dispensing under the federal rule?
questions.legal_decision: Separate partial fulfillment from refills and expiry.
questions.critical_exception: Zero authorized refills does not prevent partial fulfillment of original quantity under the federal rule.
questions.counterfactual_flip: After six months from issuance no further partial dispensing is allowed under this prescription.
questions.stem: A valid Schedule IV prescription authorizes 60 tablets with no refills. It was issued five months ago; the pharmacy has dispensed 20 tablets in a partial filling. Which statements correctly describe additional partial dispensing under the federal rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.why: Correct. All partial fills together must not exceed the original quantity.

choices.text: The six-month period restarts on the date of each partial filling.
choices.why: Incorrect. Expiration is measured from issuance.

choices.text: Subsequent partial fills must be recorded in the same manner as refills.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires refill-style recording.

choices.text: Each additional partial quantity requires a separately authorized refill.
choices.why: Incorrect. Partial fulfillment of original quantity is not a separately authorized refill.

choices.text: The remainder may be dispensed after six months if ordered before expiry.
choices.why: Incorrect. No dispensing under this provision may occur beyond six months from issuance.

questions.trigger: Which fields are expressly required on a Massachusetts pharmacy label for an ordinary human outpatient prescription for an oral liquid?

choices.why: Correct. The filling pharmacist's initials are required.

choices.text: Pharmacy name and address.
choices.why: Correct. Both are required label fields.

questions.trigger: A customer purchased 1.8 grams of pseudoephedrine base at a retail pharmacy today and returns to the same seller for 2.4 grams more. Assuming other limits are met, what additional base quantity remains under the federal daily cap, without considering package sizes?
questions.legal_decision: Apply cumulative calendar-day base limit.
questions.critical_exception: Other applicable requirements and package sizes still govern actual sales.
questions.counterfactual_flip: With no earlier purchases, 3.6 grams is the federal daily cap.
questions.stem: A customer purchased 1.8 grams of pseudoephedrine base at a retail pharmacy today and returns to the same seller for 2.4 grams more. Assuming other limits are met, what additional base quantity remains under the federal daily cap, without considering package sizes?

choices.text: 0.0 grams.
choices.why: Incorrect. The buyer has not reached the daily cap.

choices.text: 1.2 grams.
choices.why: Incorrect. This is not the remaining allowance.

choices.text: 1.8 grams.
choices.why: Correct. 3.6 grams minus the earlier 1.8 grams leaves 1.8 grams.

choices.text: 2.4 grams.
choices.why: Incorrect. This would make the total 4.2 grams.

choices.text: 3.6 grams.
choices.why: Incorrect. A second transaction does not reset the daily cap.

questions.topic: Lost blank DEA order form and recovery
questions.trigger: A pharmacy discovers that an unused DEA Form 222 is missing from its premises. Which actions are required?
questions.legal_decision: Immediately report loss and later recovery.
questions.critical_exception: Loss during transmission has a separate procedure.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An unfilled order lost in transmission is analyzed under subsection (a).
questions.stem: A pharmacy discovers that an unused DEA Form 222 is missing from its premises. Which actions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Immediately report the loss to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge.
choices.why: Correct. Loss other than in transmission must be immediately reported to the responsible SAC.

choices.text: Report the serial number if it is known.
choices.why: Correct. The number must be reported if known, with an alternative when unknown.

choices.text: Submit the report within 45 days of discovery.
choices.why: Incorrect. The reporting requirement is immediate, not 45 days.

choices.text: Immediately notify the responsible SAC if the reported unused form is recovered.
choices.why: Correct. Recovery of a reported unused form requires immediate notice.

choices.text: Report the form loss only if controlled inventory is also missing.
choices.why: Incorrect. Order-form loss has its own reporting requirement.

questions.trigger: A Massachusetts pharmacy routinely retains security-camera footage for 14 days. The pharmacist discovers credible evidence of possible controlled-substance diversion and preserves the relevant recordings. What minimum retention period applies to the recordings concerning the suspected diversion?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the special two-year video rule on suspicion.
questions.critical_exception: Confirmed theft is not necessary.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without known or suspected theft/diversion the ordinary minimum is 14 days.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy routinely retains security-camera footage for 14 days. The pharmacist discovers credible evidence of possible controlled-substance diversion and preserves the relevant recordings. What minimum retention period applies to the recordings concerning the suspected diversion?

choices.text: 14 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fourteen days is the ordinary minimum, not the special diversion rule.

choices.text: 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Thirty days is not the prescribed period.

choices.text: 90 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Ninety days is not the prescribed period.

choices.text: One year.
choices.why: Incorrect. The special minimum is longer than one year.

choices.text: Two years.
choices.why: Correct. Known or suspected theft or diversion requires at least two years of retention.

questions.topic: Accuracy assessment of automated sterile compounding device
questions.trigger: How often must personnel assess an automated sterile compounding device's accuracy when it is used?
questions.legal_decision: Assess accuracy before first use and each day used.
questions.critical_exception: Manufacturer/FDA validation does not replace the facility assessment.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A day on which the device is not used for CSPs does not trigger the daily-use assessment.
questions.stem: How often must personnel assess an automated sterile compounding device's accuracy when it is used?

choices.text: Before installation and after each annual certification.
choices.why: Incorrect. Annual certification does not meet the daily-use requirement.

choices.text: Before first use and each day of compounding use.
choices.why: Correct. USP's official FAQ specifies both initial and daily-use assessment.

choices.text: At the beginning of every calendar month of operation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Monthly assessment is insufficient on intervening days of use.

choices.text: After equipment repair and before each annual certification.
choices.why: Incorrect. Repair-related assessment does not replace the daily requirement.

choices.text: Before first use and every six months of operation thereafter.
choices.why: Incorrect. The interval is not six months.

questions.trigger: A facility prepares immediate-use CSPs under USP <797>. Its current procedure sets a one-hour administration limit. The designated person proposes changing to the chapter's maximum. Which statements are correct?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish maximum from stricter SOP and training.
questions.critical_exception: All immediate-use conditions and applicable stricter requirements still apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Category 1 or 2 compounding personnel are subject to other competency provisions.
questions.stem: A facility prepares immediate-use CSPs under USP <797>. Its current procedure sets a one-hour administration limit. The designated person proposes changing to the chapter's maximum. Which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The facility may retain its existing one-hour limit.
choices.why: Correct. USP FAQ 38 permits a stricter one-hour limit.

choices.text: A four-hour maximum is permissible if all immediate-use conditions are met.
choices.why: Correct. The chapter's maximum addressed by the FAQ is four hours.

choices.text: Personnel who prepare only immediate-use CSPs are exempt from aseptic competency.
choices.why: Incorrect. Task-appropriate aseptic competency still applies.

choices.text: Section 1.3 specifies six-month competency testing for immediate-use-only personnel.
choices.why: Incorrect. The FAQ states that section 1.3 does not set a specific frequency for this group.

choices.text: Competency must relate to assigned tasks and facility procedures.
choices.why: Correct. The training and assessment must be task- and SOP-appropriate.

questions.topic: Central fill pharmacy records for Schedule II order
questions.trigger: A retail pharmacy sends a valid Schedule II prescription to an authorized central fill pharmacy for dispensing. Which records must the central fill pharmacy itself maintain under the federal central-fill provision?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish central-fill records from retail records.
questions.critical_exception: This is central fill, not an independent prescription transfer.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For retail receipt documentation the retail employee name is required.
questions.stem: A retail pharmacy sends a valid Schedule II prescription to an authorized central fill pharmacy for dispensing. Which records must the central fill pharmacy itself maintain under the federal central-fill provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Retail pharmacy name, address and DEA number in the transmitted record.
choices.why: Correct. These identifiers are part of the central fill record.

choices.text: Name of the retail employee accepting the completed prescription at the retail location.
choices.why: Incorrect. This is the retail pharmacy's receipt record under subsection (a)(4).

choices.text: Date prescription information was received, filling pharmacist and filling date.
choices.why: Correct. Central fill must maintain these under subsection (b)(2).

choices.text: Delivery date to the retail pharmacy and method of delivery.
choices.why: Correct. Central fill retains these under subsection (b)(3).

choices.text: The original signed paper prescription as the central fill pharmacy's original record.
choices.why: Incorrect. Retail retains the original; central fill keeps a copy or electronic record as applicable.

questions.trigger: The Board returns a submitted pharmacy plan of correction because it fails to meet regulatory requirements. What is the timeframe for submitting the revised plan?
questions.legal_decision: Differentiate initial and revised deadlines.
questions.critical_exception: The initial deadline is 21 days or as directed by the Board.
questions.counterfactual_flip: On the first submission after a deficiency report use the initial-plan rule.
questions.stem: The Board returns a submitted pharmacy plan of correction because it fails to meet regulatory requirements. What is the timeframe for submitting the revised plan?

choices.text: Within seven days.
choices.why: Correct. The revision must be submitted within seven days.

choices.text: Within 14 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Fourteen days is not the revision deadline.

choices.text: Within 21 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Twenty-one days is the ordinary initial-plan deadline unless otherwise directed.

choices.text: Within 30 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Thirty days exceeds the specified revision period.

choices.text: Within 60 days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Sixty days is not the specified revision period.
